intro.text: 今天的 feed 有一条很鲜明的共同线索：AI 正在从“帮我完成任务”走向“替我判断怎么做”。Aaron Levie 说 agent 已经开始处理人类自己都难以定义的问题；Guillermo Rauch 展示了个人 agent 如何从 demo 变成可控的平台；而 Linear COO Cristina Cordova 的经验提醒我们，真正的增长仍然来自一步步找到能被组织承接的目标。

archive.title: Agent 放权日报
archive.desc: 从 agent 自主解决问题，到个人 agent 的基础设施和企业级治理，今天的主线是：能力变强之后，怎么把自由度变成可靠的工作流。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-11-21 source feeds.

sections.title: Agents Get More Room to Think / Agent 开始获得更大自主权
sections.desc: 能力跃迁的关键，不只是回答更快，而是 agent 能在更大的解空间里自己找到方案。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie argues that the best use of agents is increasingly not giving them a precise recipe, but giving them a goal they can solve better than we could. As models connect more relevant knowledge than any one person can hold, the human job shifts from specifying every step to setting direction and deciding how much freedom to grant.

That is a meaningful change in product design: agents are moving from obedient interfaces toward exploratory collaborators, especially in finance, legal, life sciences, and cybersecurity where the problem itself is hard to fully define.
original: This year we’ve had a clear jump in model capability where instead of telling agents precisely what to do, it’s better to use these systems to solve problems you can’t easily define yourself. A year ago you’d need to very clearly tell agents the how to design and develop your product idea, or there was almost no chance of success. Now, increasingly, the agent likely can come up with a better implementation than you’d have thought of because you can have it connect the dots between a far greater solution space than you can. This will be increasingly true in basically every domain of kneeler work. We’re going to see this impact in finance, legal, life sciences, cyber, and many other spaces where no person can hold onto all the available relevant industry knowledge to think of the best solution. Ultimately this is going to reshape our relationship with AI and how we deploy agents in our work. It won’t be about explicitly telling them, but instead giving them goals and enough freedom to pursue them in the best way they can.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 的判断是，agent 最有价值的用法越来越不是照着人类写好的步骤执行，而是给它一个目标，让它在更大的解空间里自己找到更好的方案。模型能连接的相关知识，已经超过单个人可以长期装在脑子里的范围，所以人的工作会从规定每一步，转向设定方向、决定该给 agent 多大自由度。
这会直接改变产品设计：agent 不再只是听话的界面，而开始成为会探索的协作者，尤其适合金融、法律、生命科学和网络安全这类连问题都很难完整定义的领域。
original: 今年模型能力有了明显跃迁：与其精确告诉 agent 怎么做，不如让它解决那些你自己都很难定义清楚的问题。以前你必须明确告诉 agent 如何设计和开发产品想法，现在 agent 越来越可能给出比你原本想到的更好实现，因为它能在比你更大的解空间里连接信息。最终，我们和 AI 的关系会改变：不再是明确指挥每一步，而是给它目标和足够的自由，让它用最好的方式完成。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch describes a personal shopper agent as his original 'hello world' for Eve. What changed is not one magical demo, but the missing stack around it: AgentCard, better models, mature iMessage and WhatsApp channels, and stronger performance without giving up durability or encryption.

The interesting point is that the platform now lets builders ship a controlled, personal version of products like Muse or Instinct instead of merely trying a chatbot. The invitation is practical: run the template, then make it your own.
original: When I first tried an internal pre-release version of @eve, a personal shopper agent was my "hello world". It worked, but a lot of the infrastructure was missing. Now, @agentcardhq exists, models are better, iMessage and WhatsApp eve channels are mature, and performance is vastly improved (without trading off durability and encryption.) The result is you can ship a platform of the caliber of Muse / Instinct, that you fully control, on our open intelligence stack. The experience is pure delight. I highly recommend you try this. Run with this template. Make it your own.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 把 personal shopper agent 当作 Eve 最初的“hello world”。真正发生变化的不是某个神奇 demo，而是它周围缺失的那层基础设施补齐了：AgentCard、更强的模型、成熟的 iMessage 和 WhatsApp channel，以及不牺牲 durability 和 encryption 的性能提升。
这意味着 builder 现在可以做出一套自己完全控制的个人 agent 平台，而不只是试用一个 chatbot。最值得注意的动作很简单：先跑起来，再把它改成自己的东西。
original: 我第一次试用 Eve 的内部预发布版本时，personal shopper agent 是我的“hello world”。它能工作，但缺了很多基础设施。现在有了 AgentCard，模型更好了，iMessage 和 WhatsApp channel 也成熟了，性能大幅提升，同时没有牺牲 durability 和 encryption。结果是，你可以在我们的 open intelligence stack 上，做出 Muse / Instinct 级别、完全由自己控制的平台。

sections.title: The Reliability Layer / 可靠性开始成为产品
sections.desc: agent 能做什么只是第一层，企业真正要买单的是它是否可审计、可治理、可稳定运行。

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch calls ISO 42001:2023 the 'SOC2 of AI': a global, independently audited standard for how companies build, evaluate, monitor, and govern AI systems. His point is less about a compliance badge than about making the infrastructure layer legible to customers who need to trust it.
original: ISO 42001:2023 is like the "SOC2 of AI". It's the first global, independently audited standard for how companies build, evaluate, monitor and govern AI systems. When you ship on and use Vercel's AI, you now know the infra is audited annually by an accredited third party.

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch 把 ISO 42001:2023 称为“AI 的 SOC2”：一套全球性的、经过独立审计的标准，用来规范企业如何构建、评估、监控和治理 AI 系统。重点不只是多一个合规徽章，而是让客户终于能看懂并信任 agent 背后的基础设施。
original: ISO 42001:2023 就像“AI 的 SOC2”。它是第一套全球性的、经过独立审计的标准，规定企业如何构建、评估、监控和治理 AI 系统。现在，在 Vercel AI 上发布和使用产品，你知道这套基础设施每年都会由获认可的第三方审计。

rewrite: Peter Yang shares a useful workaround for Antigravity users: add the web experience to your phone's home screen and use it as a remote control for all your threads. His comparison is specific: because the threads are available by default, he finds the remote-control workflow better than Claude's current mobile experience, even without a native app.
original: For those of you trying out @antigravity for Neon, here's a quick tip: 1. Go to https://t.co/GRhlnGkO1i 2. Tap see more and then the share button 3. Tap Add to Home Screen Then you can talk to all your Antigravity threads via remote control on mobile. Even though Antigravity doesn't have a mobile app (yet), I find its remote control actually better than Claude's because all the threads are available by default.

rewrite: Peter Yang 分享了一个 Antigravity 的实用 workaround：把网页体验添加到手机主屏幕，就能把手机当成所有 thread 的 remote control。这个细节很重要：虽然 Antigravity 还没有原生 mobile app，但因为所有 thread 默认都可用，他觉得这套远程控制体验反而比 Claude 当前的移动端更好。
original: 如果你在用 Antigravity for Neon，这里有个小技巧：打开链接，点击 see more，再点分享，然后选择 Add to Home Screen。这样你就能在手机上通过 remote control 和所有 Antigravity thread 对话。虽然 Antigravity 还没有 mobile app，但因为所有 thread 默认都可用，我觉得它的 remote control 其实比 Claude 的更好。

sections.title: Build for the Workflow, Not the Demo / 产品要进入真实工作流
sections.desc: 今天几个 builder 的共同提醒是：用户不会为“看起来像 AI”付费，而会为真正改变工作方式的细节留下来。

rewrite: Zara Zhang gives a sharp warning to AI consultants and product builders: don't hand clients a raw Claude Artifact or ChatGPT site. If the deliverable looks like something the client could have prompted themselves, you have exposed the lack of product value. The wrapper needs to encode judgment, workflow, or execution, not merely display a model response.
original: Do not send your clients Claude Artifacts/ChatGPT sites It makes them feel like "Well I could have just prompted Claude/Codex myself"

rewrite: Zara Zhang 给 AI 顾问和 builder 提了个很尖锐的醒：不要把原始的 Claude Artifact 或 ChatGPT site 直接交给客户。如果交付物看起来只是客户自己 prompt 一下就能得到的东西，你等于主动暴露了产品价值的缺失。真正的价值应该藏在判断、工作流和执行里，而不是只展示一段模型输出。
original: 不要把 Claude Artifacts / ChatGPT sites 发给客户。客户会觉得：“那我自己 prompt Claude/Codex 不就行了？”

rewrite: Matt Turck tells a small but revealing story about automated agentic email: an agent sent several messages to arrange a meeting, then failed to recognize the person in real life. The joke lands because the automation optimized for message cadence while missing the actual social context. Agentic workflows still need identity, memory, and a handoff to reality.
original: Automated agentic emailing vs the real world, a story: Guy emails me twice to meet at a conference (Slush) I reply once He then emails me 3 times in rapid succession Damn that guy really wants to meet I bump into him later that day I say “well, was meant to be” He reads my name tag, twice. Blank face. He clearly has no idea who I am. He says “oh hi” and walks away. The end.

rewrite: Matt Turck 讲了个关于 agentic email 的小故事：agent 为了约会议连续发了几封邮件，但在线下碰面时却完全没认出对方。好笑之处也正是问题所在：自动化优化了消息频率，却没有理解真实的社交上下文。agent workflow 还需要 identity、memory，以及和现实世界之间更聪明的 handoff。
original: 自动化 agentic emailing 对上现实世界：一个人给我发了两封邮件约 Slush 见面，我回了一封；然后他又在很短时间内连发三封。我后来在线下遇到他，说“看来我们注定要见面”，他看了我的名牌两遍，满脸空白，显然完全不知道我是谁。他说“哦，你好”，然后走了。故事结束。

rewrite: The takeaway from Linear COO Cristina Cordova is that scaling is not a license to hire executives early; it is a process of discovering which capability the company can actually support. Linear moved from a product-led motion toward larger customers by setting a solvable near-term goal, then using a real go-to-market project as a work trial for the person who would own it.

Her most useful distinction is between selling to companies that are growing into your product and convincing an existing company to rip out a system it already trusts. The latter requires product strength, references, and organizational readiness, not just a bigger sales target.
original: I generally don't believe every company needs a COO. ... You have to really understand as a founder, what are the things you need and what are the things you're looking for in the people that you bring onto the team?

The good thing about that is that, you know, that is the job. ... You're not giving someone some fictional project that's not really like representative of what they would do when they join the company.

rewrite: Linear COO Cristina Cordova 的核心经验是：公司开始增长，不等于马上该招一个 COO；真正重要的是先找出组织当前能承接的能力。Linear 从 product-led motion 走向更大客户时，先把目标改成一个可解决的近场问题，再用真实的 go-to-market 项目作为候选人的 work trial。
她区分了两种完全不同的销售：让正在成长的公司自然用上你的产品，和说服一家已经信任旧系统的公司把它拆掉重来。后者需要产品优势、客户口碑和组织准备度，不只是把销售目标写得更大。
original: 我通常不认为每家公司都需要 COO。创始人必须真正理解：你需要什么，以及你希望带进团队的人解决什么问题？
好处是，这本身就是工作。你不是给候选人一个和入职后工作无关的虚构项目。
